overview: AUX Electric is a Chinese household and central air-conditioner manufacturer founded in 1994 in Ningbo, Zhejiang, with design, R&D, manufacturing, sales and after-sales service integrated under one roof. It is the world's fifth-largest air-conditioner supplier by sales volume, selling household (wall-mounted, cabinet, mobile) and central (VRF, packaged units, heat pumps, chillers) air conditioners under a multi-brand portfolio (AUX, Hutssom, AUFIT, ShinFlow) plus a large ODM export business, to more than 160 countries and regions. The company listed on the HKEX Main Board on September 2, 2025 (stock code 2580), raising roughly HK$3.6-4.2 billion in what was reported as the largest Hong Kong IPO debut of 2025; it reports in RMB while trading in HKD, and as a brand-new listing has only three filings (Annual FY2025, H1 FY2025, H1 FY2026) with no pre-IPO quarterly/annual history.

business_model.summary: AUX generates revenue almost entirely from manufacturing and selling air conditioners: ~87-89% from household air conditioners (wall-mounted, cabinet-style, mobile) and ~10-11% from central/commercial air conditioners (VRF, heat pumps, chillers), plus a small 'other business' line. Within that, revenue splits between four owned brands sold mostly through its pioneering 'Hello AUX' online wholesale new-retail model (direct factory-to-store, cutting out distribution layers) and a large ODM (original design manufacturer) export business that leverages cost/scale advantages for third-party brands. Roughly half of revenue is domestic (Chinese Mainland ~51%) and half international (Asia ex-China, Europe, North America, South America, other), making it a largely transactional, unit-sale (not recurring/subscription) hardware business with seasonal demand tied to summer cooling seasons and, in China, government trade-in subsidy cycles.

revenue_streams.name: Household air conditioners (wall-mounted/cabinet/mobile)
revenue_streams.trend: pressured - declined 14.1% YoY in H1 FY2026

revenue_streams.name: Central/commercial air conditioners (VRF, heat pumps, chillers)
revenue_streams.trend: growth initiative, higher margin (~31% GM vs ~16% household)

revenue_streams.name: Other business
revenue_streams.trend: small but growing, 47% YoY H1 FY2026

revenue_streams.name: ODM (third-party brand export manufacturing)
revenue_streams.trend: declining - down 24.7% YoY in H1 FY2026, largest single swing factor

revenue_streams.name: AUFIT (new sub-brand, online-focused)
revenue_streams.trend: fast growing - up 79% YoY in H1 FY2026

business_model.customer_type: Mixed B2B/B2C: direct-to-consumer retail via owned brands and online channels (Douyin, Meituan, JD, WeChat ecosystem) plus large B2B ODM relationships manufacturing for other brands/export customers; also project-based sales for commercial/central air-conditioning (hotels, hospitals, municipal, data centres)
business_model.geographic_mix: Chinese Mainland ~51% (FY2025), Asia ex-China ~27%, Europe ~9-10%, North America ~5-7%, South America ~5%, other ~2%; overseas revenue is approximately 50% of total, with ODM/export tied closely to US dollar, euro, yen and Thai baht exposure

competitive_position.market_position: Value/mass-market challenger brand - world's fifth-largest air-conditioner maker by volume and ranked among the global top three/four in household split-unit sales in recent years, but a fraction of the scale of the 'big three' (Midea, Gree, Haier), which together hold roughly 70%+ of China's retail air-conditioner volume. AUX has built share with the lowest average selling price among the top five Chinese makers, competing on cost and online-direct distribution rather than premium positioning.

moat_factors.factor: Low-cost online wholesale distribution model ('Hello AUX')
moat_factors.description: Industry-first online wholesale new-retail model cuts out traditional distribution layers, giving a structural cost advantage and fast scale-up versus traditional multi-tier dealer networks
May 2025 Wuhu compressor plant (Panasonic technology) makes AUX only the third air-conditioner maker with in-house compressor R&D/manufacturing, reducing a key supply-chain dependency
Strong ODM cost competitiveness and delivery capability supports third-party brand manufacturing relationships, though this revenue stream is volatile and lower-margin

AUX brand recognized for value/smart features (No.1 in smart voice-controlled AC sales 2022-2024) but sits below Midea/Gree/Haier in prestige; multi-brand matrix (AUX/Hutssom/AUFIT/ShinFlow) is an attempt to move upmarket

1,600+ person global R&D team, 3,200+ maintained invention patents, three R&D centres (Ningbo, Zhuhai, Japan), but has been embroiled in IP litigation with Gree in both directions (won and lost cases), indicating technology leadership is contested rather than dominant

weaknesses: Sub-scale versus Midea/Gree/Haier, limiting purchasing power and pricing leverage in a capital- and raw-material-intensive industry
Heavy reliance on ODM/export manufacturing (39% of FY2025 revenue) which is low-margin, volatile and highly exposed to tariffs, freight disruption and FX

Household air conditioners (87% of revenue) carry structurally lower gross margins (~15-16% in H1 FY2026) than central air conditioning (~28-31%), leaving overall profitability vulnerable to price wars
History of IP/trade-secret litigation with Gree (both directions) signals ongoing competitive friction and legal cost/overhang risk
Thin post-IPO trading and filing history (only 3 filings) limits long-term track record investors can assess

growth_drivers: Internationalisation strategy: establishing 3-5 new overseas sales companies per year (5 added in 2025 in Vietnam, Saudi Arabia, Dubai, Italy, Spain; 10 countries covered by H1 FY2026), targeting untapped large markets such as Japan, Indonesia and Argentina
Brand premiumisation via multi-tier portfolio - AUFIT (youth/online, +79% YoY H1 FY2026) and ShinFlow (premium) aimed at lifting blended ASP and margin mix away from commoditized ODM/value segment

Central/commercial air-conditioning expansion (VRF X9 series, data centre and liquid-cooling solutions, heavy commercial heat pumps) - a structurally higher-margin segment the company is explicitly prioritizing for 2026

AI/smart technology integration (voice control via Baidu/Alibaba/DeepSeek partnerships, AIoT, HarmonyOS/Huawei ecosystem linkage) to shift products from 'value-for-money' to 'intelligence-driven value' positioning and support pricing power
In-house compressor manufacturing (Wuhu plant, commenced May 2025) reducing supply-chain dependency and potentially improving unit economics

Domestic channel digitalisation (cloud warehouse system launched May 2026, AUX Manager dashboard, Douyin/Meituan/Amap instant-retail partnerships) to improve working-capital efficiency and terminal-store productivity
Product category expansion via OEM/brand-licensing into adjacent home appliance categories, leveraging existing channel and brand resources
Capital markets access post-IPO: proceeds earmarked ~50% for manufacturing/supply-chain upgrades, ~20% for R&D, ~20% for sales channels, ~10% working capital

business.description: Management explicitly flags price-war risk in both FY2025 and H1 FY2026 filings; intensified competition in the replacement market compressed gross margin from 21.0% (FY2024) to 18.8% (FY2025) to 18.1% (H1 FY2026)
ODM (39% of FY2025 revenue) fell 24.7% YoY in H1 FY2026, the single largest driver of the revenue decline, reflecting dependence on third-party brand order cycles outside AUX's direct control
Heavy reliance on domestic online/offline retail channels and China's subsidy-driven replacement cycle; withdrawal of trade-in subsidies cited as a 2025 headwind
History of patent and trade-secret litigation with Gree (AUX has both won and lost cases, including a compressor patent later invalidated), indicating ongoing legal and competitive friction risk

financial.description: Nearly 50% of revenue is overseas in USD, EUR, JPY, THB and other currencies while reporting in RMB; RMB appreciation was explicitly cited as reducing H1 FY2026 overseas revenue and margins; hedging only partially mitigates this
H1 FY2026 free cash flow fell sharply to RMB147m from RMB1,260m a year earlier due to higher capex and seasonal working-capital unwind, illustrating cash-flow volatility around the half-year cycle

Total debt rose from RMB1,553m (FY2024) to RMB2,533m (H1 FY2026) as the company funds capacity expansion (Wuhu compressor plant, overseas sales companies), though cash balances (RMB7.7bn) comfortably exceed debt

regulatory.description: Management explicitly flags risk of increased US and other major-economy tariffs and retaliatory trade measures raising export costs and compressing margins/order volume

regulatory.risk: Geopolitical/trade barrier risk in overseas markets
regulatory.description: Local permits, licensing, foreign exchange controls, political unrest and tax law changes in the 160+ countries AUX sells into
Withdrawal of national trade-in subsidy support was cited as a 2025 headwind for domestic replacement demand

macro.description: Ongoing Middle East conflict explicitly cited as suppressing H1 FY2026 regional demand (Asia ex-China revenue down 18.8%, the single largest swing factor) and disrupting shipping routes/freight costs
Copper, aluminium, steel, plastics, compressor and motor costs are key inputs; rising prices repeatedly cited as a gross-margin headwind across FY2025 and H1 FY2026

macro.risk: Weak global consumer demand / weather cyclicality
macro.description: Air-conditioner demand is highly weather- and macro-cycle dependent; China retail volumes fell 13.1% YoY in H1 FY2026 amid subdued consumer demand, while elevated channel inventory persists in Eastern Europe and Latin America

macro_factors.industry_outlook: Chinese air-conditioner industry is mature and increasingly saturated domestically (China retail volume -1.3% in 2025, H1 FY2026 China retail volume -13.1% YoY) with growth now driven mainly by replacement cycles, AI/smart features and export/overseas expansion; overseas emerging markets (Southeast Asia, Middle East) remain structural growth areas for AUX despite near-term geopolitical disruption, while developed markets (Europe, North America) are more volatile
macro_factors.cyclicality: High - demand is weather-dependent (summer temperatures), tied to China property/renovation cycles, and sensitive to government subsidy programs (trade-in policy); also exposed to China's broader macro/consumer-spending cycle
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: Low-moderate direct exposure (modest bank borrowings, finance costs ~RMB57m in FY2025), but higher-rate environments could pressure channel partners' working capital and consumer financing for large-ticket purchases

recent_developments.event: AUX Electric listed on HKEX Main Board, raising approximately HK$3.6-4.2 billion in what was reported as Hong Kong's largest IPO debut of 2025; shares fell on the first trading day
Wuhu compressor plant (Panasonic technology) commenced production, making AUX the third air-conditioner maker with in-house compressor R&D/manufacturing capability

Profit warning/positive-profit announcement ahead of FY2025 results flagged profit attributable to owners falling to approximately RMB2.2 billion from RMB2.9 billion in 2024, citing rising raw material prices, high channel inventory, weak consumer demand, intensified domestic competition and pricing pressure; shares fell roughly 10-11% on the announcement
Cloud warehouse system officially launched, rolled out in Zhejiang, Jiangxi and Guangxi, aimed at improving inventory turnover and fulfilment efficiency
Board changes: Ms. TANG Mei Shan appointed independent non-executive director; Mr. TAO Shengwen retired from the Board (June 5, 2026)

H1 FY2026 interim results: revenue down 12.9% YoY to RMB17,503.7m, profit attributable to owners down 40.8% YoY to RMB1,107.9m; gross margin compressed to 18.1% from 19.5%; decline attributed to Middle East geopolitical conflict, subdued domestic demand, RMB appreciation and elevated raw material (copper) costs; free cash flow fell sharply to RMB147m from RMB1,260m a year earlier on higher capex and working-capital unwind

items.target: no less than 75% of net profit attributable to owners
items.notes: Board-announced minimum payout commitment for each of 2025, 2026 and 2027, signalling capital-return priority despite declining earnings

items.target: 3-5 new overseas sales companies per year
items.notes: Consistent target reiterated in both FY2025 annual report and H1 FY2026 interim; 5 added in 2025, bringing total countries with sales companies to 10 by H1 FY2026

items.metric: Strategic priority: overseas 'scale + profit' dual enhancement
items.target: qualitative - shift overseas strategy from pure scale expansion to combined scale and profitability
items.vs_prior: new framing introduced in H1 FY2026
items.notes: Management commentary signals a pivot toward margin discipline in overseas markets given FX and geopolitical headwinds

items.metric: No formal revenue/EPS numeric guidance disclosed
items.notes: Company does not publish formal quantitative revenue/profit guidance; third-party analyst estimates (e.g., Huaxi Securities) reportedly project FY2026 net profit around RMB2.2 billion, implying a stronger H2 to offset the H1 decline, but this is not company-issued guidance

guidance.management_commentary: Management across both FY2025 and H1 FY2026 filings consistently describes 2025-2026 as a period of 'external uncertainty' from tariffs, geopolitical conflict (Middle East), RMB appreciation and intensified domestic price competition, but expresses confidence in the company's 'efficient decision-making, rapid response and strong execution,' citing prior cycle resilience. Strategic priorities reiterated: internationalisation, multi-brand premiumisation (AUFIT, ShinFlow), central air-conditioning expansion, and new home-appliance category entry via OEM/licensing.

bull_case: Deep value entry point post-IPO: shares have traded well below the IPO range/52-week high (~HK$9-11 vs IPO price ~HK$16-17.4 and a 52-week high near HK$16.79), with reported consensus analyst price targets implying meaningful upside and a 'Strong Buy' rating from the (small) covering analyst base

Structural overseas growth runway: emerging markets (Southeast Asia, Middle East, and new entries like Japan/Indonesia/Argentina) remain underpenetrated for AUX's value-oriented brand, with a replicable 'Hello AUX' localisation playbook and 10 overseas sales companies already established

Margin-mix upside from central air-conditioning and premium sub-brands: central AC carries roughly double the gross margin of household units, and AUFIT/ShinFlow are growing fast off a small base, which could lift blended profitability if the mix shift continues
Vertically integrated supply chain (in-house compressors from May 2025) and heavy R&D/patent investment support medium-term cost and differentiation advantages versus smaller value competitors
Committed capital return policy (minimum 75% payout through FY2027) provides a visible income floor for shareholders even through a cyclical earnings downturn, provided free cash flow holds up
bear_case: Earnings momentum is clearly negative and company-flagged: FY2025 net profit fell 23.2% and H1 FY2026 net profit fell 40.8% YoY, with management itself warning (March 2026) of results below the prior year before the drop was confirmed
Heavy and volatile ODM exposure (39-44% of revenue) ties results to third-party brand order cycles and tariff/trade-policy risk outside AUX's control; ODM revenue fell nearly 25% YoY in H1 FY2026

Structural competitive disadvantage versus Midea/Gree/Haier, which together command the large majority of China's air-conditioner market with far greater scale, pricing power and brand equity, while Xiaomi is also encroaching on the value segment AUX occupies

Multiple simultaneous macro headwinds (RMB appreciation, Middle East conflict, elevated raw material/copper costs, China demand softness, tariff risk) are all pressuring the business concurrently with no clear near-term resolution, and H1 FY2026 free cash flow collapsed to RMB147m from RMB1,260m

Very short public trading/filing history (IPO September 2025, only 3 filings) limits investors' ability to assess management's capital-allocation discipline and the durability of the dividend commitment through a full cycle
